identification.summary: Russian covert influence operation that Microsoft's Threat Analysis Center (MTAC) tracked as Storm-1516 and described as Kremlin-aligned [S1][S2]. Its signature is a fabricated video, often with a paid actor posing as a whistleblower or citizen journalist, laundered through newly created websites that imitate local or well-known media outlets and then amplified by influencers [S1][S2][S9]. France's VIGINUM analyzed 77 Storm-1516 operations documented from the operation's emergence through 5 March 2025 [S8]. NewsGuard assessed in December 2025 that Storm-1516 had overtaken Russian state media (RT and Sputnik) as the leading source of false Russia-Ukraine claims it tracks, based on roughly 400 debunked narratives [S6][S7].
identification.firstObserved: VIGINUM dates the operation's start to March 2023 [S8].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Neva Flood (formerly Storm-1516), per the encyclopedia's imported Microsoft naming mapping; not re-verified in this research pass. Recorded Future tracks a closely related network as CopyCop, which it links to John Mark Dougan, the Moscow-based Center for Geopolitical Expertise (CGE) and the GRU [S4][S5]. VIGINUM treats Storm-1516 and CopyCop as overlapping rather than identical, and links Storm-1516 to sub-clusters including former Prigozhin troll-farm staff and Dougan's fake-news sites [S8]. Keep CopyCop website counts and Storm-1516 operation counts separate.

attribution.sponsor: Russian Federation. VIGINUM attributes central coordination to Yury Khoroshenky, whom it describes as a suspected officer of Russian military intelligence (GRU) [S8]. The US Treasury said the GRU directed and funded the CGE and US-based facilitators who built an AI server and at least 100 imitation news websites for 2024 US election interference [S10]. The EU sanctioned Dougan in December 2025 as responsible for the Storm-1516 campaign, and the German government publicly blamed Russia for using Storm-1516 against its federal election [S11].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft (MTAC) labels Storm-1516 Kremlin-aligned [S1][S2]. VIGINUM (French government) states its investigations confirm involvement of individuals and organizations close to the Russian state, including Dougan [S8]. Recorded Future assesses CopyCop is very likely operated by Dougan with CGE and GRU support [S4][S5]. Treasury's December 2024 designation of the CGE describes a GRU-funded website network but, in the coverage reviewed, does not name Storm-1516 or Dougan [S10]. Dougan denies working for the Russian government [S3].
attribution.basis: Microsoft MTAC election reporting [S1][S2]; VIGINUM technical report (via secondary coverage) [S8]; Recorded Future Insikt Group CopyCop reporting [S4][S5]; US Treasury OFAC sanctions on CGE and Valery Korovin (via press coverage) [S10]; EU sanctions and German government statement (via CORRECTIV) [S11]; investigative reporting by CORRECTIV [S3].

objectives: Undermine Western support for Ukraine and shape elections in target countries in Russia's favor [S1][S9]. Bloomberg's 2026 analysis of Storm-1516 videos found more than 40% aimed at undermining support for Ukraine and about one-third targeted elections in countries other than the US [S9]. NewsGuard found false narratives aimed at France closely followed French expressions of support for Ukraine [S7].

sectors: News media (impersonation of outlets and real journalists) [S1][S4]
regions: Ukraine (narratives about Ukraine and its leadership) [S6][S9]
targeting.notes: Targets track Russian foreign-policy priorities: the US election in 2024, then Germany ahead of its February 2025 election, and France following its support for Ukraine [S1][S3][S7]. Canada and Moldova targeting is from Recorded Future's CopyCop reporting, an overlapping cluster [S4].

capabilities.summary: Production of staged or AI-manipulated videos featuring actors posing as whistleblowers or citizen journalists [S1][S9]. Rapid creation of fake news websites that imitate local outlets, sometimes registered only days before use, with large reserves of dormant sites prepared in advance (more than 100 German-named sites before the 2025 election) [S1][S2][S3]. Generative AI used to rewrite the same story for each site [S3]; Recorded Future reports self-hosted, uncensored Llama 3 models, likely GRU-financed, and over 300 inauthentic CopyCop websites in 2025 [S4]. Impersonation of media outlets, political parties, fact-checkers and real journalists [S4]. Amplification through pro-Russian influencers, Telegram channels and hashtags on X [S2][S3].

campaigns.name: Operation start (VIGINUM)
campaigns.summary: VIGINUM dates the first Storm-1516 information operation to March 2023 [S8].

campaigns.name: CopyCop website surge
campaigns.summary: Recorded Future reported the CopyCop network registered 120 new websites between 10 and 12 May 2024 and used more than 1,000 fake journalist personas, expanding into US election content [S5].

campaigns.name: Harris hit-and-run fabrication
campaigns.summary: MTAC attributed to Storm-1516 a video in which an actor falsely claimed Kamala Harris had been in a 2011 hit-and-run, laundered through a fake San Francisco outlet created days earlier; it drew millions of views [S1][S2].

campaigns.name: US sanctions on CGE
campaigns.summary: Treasury sanctioned the Center for Geopolitical Expertise and its director Valery Korovin for GRU-directed, AI-enabled disinformation against the 2024 US election [S10].

campaigns.name: German federal election network
campaigns.summary: CORRECTIV and partners exposed more than 100 German-named fake news sites tied to Storm-1516, many dormant and pre-positioned, pushing fabricated allegations against politicians, including Robert Habeck [S3].

campaigns.name: VIGINUM technical report
campaigns.summary: France's VIGINUM published an analysis of 77 Storm-1516 operations documented through 5 March 2025 and named suspected GRU officer Yury Khoroshenky as a central figure [S8].

campaigns.name: CopyCop expansion
campaigns.summary: Recorded Future reported at least 200 new CopyCop websites in 2025, bringing the year's total above 300, and self-hosted Llama 3 models [S4].

campaigns.name: EU sanctions on Dougan
campaigns.summary: The EU sanctioned John Mark Dougan as responsible for the Storm-1516 campaign, after Germany blamed Russia for using it against its election and summoned the Russian ambassador [S11].

campaigns.name: NewsGuard 400-claim assessment
campaigns.summary: NewsGuard found Russian influence operations, led by Storm-1516, overtook state media as the largest source of false Russia-Ukraine claims in 2025 [S6][S7].

diamond.adversary: Russian state-linked operators. VIGINUM names suspected GRU officer Yury Khoroshenky as coordinator [S8]. US-born Russia resident John Mark Dougan, sanctioned by the EU, produces content [S3][S11]. The GRU-funded CGE is sanctioned by Treasury [S10].
diamond.capability: Staged or AI-manipulated videos with paid actors [S1][S9]. AI-rewritten articles [S3]. Self-hosted Llama 3 content generation [S4]. Impersonation of outlets and journalists [S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Hundreds of imitation news domains, many created days before use or held dormant [S1][S3][S4]. Purpose-built video channels and influencer, Telegram and X amplification networks [S2][S3].
diamond.victim: Voters and information environments in the US, Germany, France, Canada and Moldova [S1][S3][S4]. Political leaders who are smeared [S1][S3]. Media brands and journalists whose identities are spoofed [S4].
diamond.socioPolitical: Erode Western support for Ukraine and influence elections toward Kremlin-preferred outcomes [S1][S7][S9].
diamond.technology: Low-cost domain registration, generative AI, and social platforms with weak provenance signals; AI chatbots that repeat the false narratives [S3][S4][S7].

gaps: Primary documents not opened (fetch failed): VIGINUM/SGDSN Storm-1516 report, Microsoft MTAC reports, Recorded Future CopyCop reports, Treasury press release. Details rely on search-result coverage.
Microsoft's renaming of Storm-1516 to Neva Flood comes from the imported Microsoft mapping and was not re-verified in this pass; no Microsoft publication using the name Neva Flood was located.
Exact publication dates of the Recorded Future reports (S4, S5) and the VIGINUM report (S8) were not confirmed against the original pages.
Boundary between Storm-1516 (Microsoft/VIGINUM) and CopyCop (Recorded Future) is unresolved; VIGINUM calls them overlapping.
Alliance4Europe and co-authors link Storm-1516 to Prigozhin's Foundation to Battle Injustice (R-FBI); that report's date and details were not verified.

The Insider and Gnida Project report 2025 Storm-1516 fabrications aimed at Moldova, Armenia and France that used real journalists' identities; not included as cited events because publication dates were not confirmed.
Secondary coverage of the VIGINUM report says Khoroshenky is possibly assigned to GRU Unit 29155; this was not confirmed in the primary report.
No MITRE ATT&CK group entry exists; the actor is an influence operation, not an intrusion set, so cyber-intrusion TTPs are not documented.
Measured effects on voter behavior or policy outcomes are not documented; reach figures (views) are vendor and media estimates.
Secondary coverage states Clemson University's Media Forensics Hub first identified the operation in December 2023, before MTAC named it; the Clemson report was not located.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (operational environment): The relevant terrain is the information environment of the US and allies that support Ukraine. This includes local-news brand trust, social platforms (X, Telegram), and AI chatbots that repeat narratives [S3][S7]. STEP 2 (effects): Pre-positioned dormant domain reserves let the actor surge within days of a political trigger, such as a coalition collapse or an election [S3]. STEP 3 (threat model): The template is fabricated video with an actor, then laundering through a fake local outlet created days earlier, then amplification by influencers and Telegram [S1][S2][S3]. STEP 4 (COAs): MLCOA is continued fabrications against leaders of pro-Ukraine states timed to aid decisions and elections [S7][S9]. MDCOA is a fabricated whistleblower video alleging misconduct by US or allied military personnel or units during a crisis, aimed at splitting coalition support. Candidate indicators: bursts of newly registered domains with local-news names, sites that share templates or AI-rewritten copy, and actor-led 'whistleblower' videos first posted on new channels [S1][S3][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track public reporting from VIGINUM, Microsoft MTAC, Recorded Future and NewsGuard, and monitor new domain registrations that imitate news outlets near allied elections [S3][S4][S8]. (2) Authorities: this is foreign malign influence aimed at civilian audiences. Response, including attribution and sanctions, has come through Treasury, the EU and allied governments, not military cyber channels [S10][S11]. DoD roles are mainly support and force protection. (3) Mission assurance: prepare rapid public-affairs and command responses to fabricated claims about personnel or operations, because fabricated videos gain millions of views quickly [S1][S2]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with allied agencies (e.g., VIGINUM) and interagency partners. Recognize vendor cluster differences (Storm-1516 vs CopyCop) when fusing reporting [S5][S8].
